title: Finite and compatible parameter-root coordinate views
statement: Let $p,r\in\mathbf N$, let $H$ be a commutative ring and $t:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to H$. Let $N_p$ be the positive orders prime to $p$, as in [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module]. For an optional order $k$, define $A_k$ to be the simultaneous root quotient $H[X_i]/(X_i^n-t_i)_i$ [def-sfb-parameter-root-algebra] if $k=n\in N_p$, and the actual compatible-root quotient $H[X_{i,n}]/(X_{i,n}^n-t_i,\ X_{i,m}^{m/n}-X_{i,n}\ (n\mid m))$ of [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module] if $k$ has no order. Its generator labels are $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ in the finite case and $\operatorname{Fin}(r)\times N_p$ in the full case. The parameter index and order of a label are respectively $i,n$, with $n=k$ at a finite level; its root is the class of its polynomial variable. The ring and coefficient-algebra structures are those of these quotients. For $S\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ and a tag $e\in\{0,1,2\}$, define the boundary ideal $J_{k,e,S}$ generated by all root coordinates with parameter index in $S$ if $e=0$, by the images of $t_i$ for $i\in S$ if $e=1$, and by the single image of $\prod_{i\in S}t_i$ if $e=2$. For an optional boundary datum $d$, set $C_{k,d}=A_k$ when $d$ is absent and $C_{k,d}=A_k/J_{k,e,S}$ when $d=(e,S)$, with its identity or quotient map $q_{k,d}$. These are the ordinary polynomial quotient and generated-ideal constructions [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $f=\prod_i t_i$. Define the view $V_{k,d,b}$ to be $C_{k,d}$ if $b$ is false and the localization $C_{k,d}[1/q_{k,d}(f)]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] if $b$ is true, with its inherited commutative ring structure and canonical map $A_k\to V_{k,d,b}$ (the quotient map followed, when necessary, by localization). This is only notation for these actual rings, coordinates and canonical maps: no transition, comparison, colimit property, or existence theorem is included. No characteristic, locality, nonzero-ring or nonempty-parameter assumption is imposed.
